problems.memo_sentence: The authors acknowledge that their approach is limited by focusing primarily on URL-based information, explicitly noting that it does not fully incorporate other informative aspects of phishing such as visual similarity of web content and user interaction behavior.
problems.source_evidence: The paper says: "Current methods frequently focus On specific aspects of phishing, including text analysis in emails or URLs. There is a severe shortage of comprehensive models that consider the various elements of phishing schemes, including attachments, URLs, sender information, images, and textual content" and later describes the proposed system as using "URLs and webpage code" plus post-deployment URL encoding.
problems.explanation: The memo invents a specific limitation about missing visual similarity and user interaction behavior that is not stated in the paper. The paper does criticize current methods for focusing on limited aspects, but it does not explicitly acknowledge those exact omissions as a limitation of this work.

problems.memo_sentence: Across four public phishing URL datasets, the proposed OptSHQCNN framework reportedly achieves very high performance, with overall accuracy, precision, recall, and F1/FI-score values above 99% and MCC around 99%, and false positive rates well below 1%. Detailed results show accuracies of 99.36% on Mendeley_2020, 99.18% on ISCX-URL-2016, 99.12% on a URL-based dataset, and 99.17% on PhishStorm, alongside low computational time (around 9–13 ms) in feature selection and optimization.
problems.source_evidence: The paper reports these results in its own tables, but the specific statement about "low computational time (around 9–13 ms) in feature selection and optimization" comes from Table 9 and is tied to the feature selection/optimization setup, not the overall framework performance claim. More importantly, the paper's abstract only says "With a maximum of above 99% accuracy, precision, recall, and Fl-score, respectively," while the detailed dataset-specific numbers appear later in the Results section.
problems.explanation: This memo sentence blends abstract-level summary with later table results and presents them as one unified reported outcome. The computational-time detail is a separate table result, not part of the same performance claim, so the attribution is overly merged and misleading.

problems.memo_sentence: The study claims that the proposed OptSHQCNN-based method outperforms a range of popular phishing detection and optimization methods, including traditional machine learning (e.g., Random Forest), deep learning variants (e.g., DNN+LSTM), and standard optimizers.
problems.source_evidence: In the Results section, the paper also reports that some baselines are quite close on certain datasets and metrics, e.g. on ISCX-URL-2016 PDSMV3-DCRNN has 99.08% accuracy versus the proposed 99.18%, and on the URL dataset LR+SVC+DT reaches 98.12% accuracy versus the proposed 99.12%.
problems.explanation: The memo correctly says the proposed method outperforms baselines overall, but it omits that the margins are sometimes small and that some baselines are near-parity on specific datasets. This is a selective presentation of the comparative results.

problems.memo_sentence: The paper positions its main contribution as a dual-phase deep learning framework (pre-deployment and post-deployment) featuring a novel OptSHQCNN pipeline that integrates advanced preprocessing, attention-based feature extraction, meta-heuristic feature selection, a shallow hybrid quantum-classical CNN classifier, and optimizer-driven hyperparameter tuning.
problems.source_evidence: The paper's Results and Discussion section adds substantial empirical detail: it reports specific dataset splits, exact metric values, optimizer comparisons, feature-selection timing, and an ablation study showing that adding more stages monotonically improves accuracy.
problems.explanation: The memo emphasizes the abstract/introduction framing and novelty claim, but it underrepresents the paper's substantial results/discussion content. This is a mild section-bias issue because the memo does include some results elsewhere, but the balance is skewed toward the front matter.
